lines.japanese: タマちゃんに理由を訊ねられて思ったこと。私はなぜ逃げたのでしょう。
lines.english: Tama asked me why, and that got me thinking. Why did I run away?

lines.japanese: 「あれじゃない」
lines.english: “Don't ‘huh’ me.”

lines.japanese: 「だよね、意味わかんないよね私」
lines.english: “Right? I don't make any sense, do I?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、意味わかんない自覚はあるんだ……」
lines.english: “Oh, so you do realize that...”

lines.japanese: 「恋愛すると頭悪くなるって本当なんだね」
lines.english: “It really is true that falling in love makes you stupid.”

lines.japanese: 「それは学習に費やす時間が減るとか、集中力が散漫になるとかって意味じゃないの？」
lines.english: “Doesn't that mean you spend less time studying, or find it harder to concentrate?”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、そうかもだけど、でもそれだけじゃないと思う」
lines.english: “Hmm, maybe, but I don't think that's all there is to it.”

lines.japanese: 「そうなの？」
lines.english: “Really?”

lines.japanese: 「うん。レンアイってゆうのはね、そんな論理的に解明できる概念じゃあなくて、もっとこう、超自然科学的な何かなんだよ」
lines.english: “Yeah. You see, this thing called love isn't a concept you can explain logically. It's more, like, something supernaturally scientific.”

lines.japanese: 「その恋愛ってゆう何かが、思考のプロセスにつるんと割りこんでくるの。『なにが』『どうして』『こうなる』の隙間に、ヒュッて勝手なピースを投げこんできちゃうの」
lines.english: “This thing called love slips right into your thought processes. Into the gaps between ‘what,’ ‘why,’ and ‘how it turns out,’ it tosses a random piece of its own. Whoosh!”

lines.japanese: 「つるんと割りこんでくる……いいねそれ。ちょうだい？」
lines.english: “Slips right in... I like that. Can I have it?”

lines.japanese: タマちゃんが使いこまれたポケット手帳を抜きだしながら言いました。それは「携帯電話のメモ機能なんてまだるっこしい」と鼻息荒く語る細川玉木せんせーが常時携行している秘伝のネタ帳なのです。
lines.english: Tama said this as she took out her well-worn pocket notebook. The secret idea book Ms. Tamaki Hosokawa always carries with her, having indignantly declared that ‘the memo function on a cell phone is too much trouble.’

lines.japanese: 「いいよー、７兆万円」
lines.english: “Suuure. Seventy quadrillion yen.”

lines.japanese: 「んー、そのうち払う」
lines.english: “Hmm, I'll pay you someday.”

lines.japanese: 適当な請求に適当な承諾が返ってきて、ちぴペンの走る音がさらさらと騒がしい教室に呑みこまれてゆきました。
lines.english: My arbitrary demand received an equally arbitrary agreement. The scratching of her little pen was swallowed up by the noisy classroom.

lines.japanese: 五時間目の休み時間、一年Ｂ組教室。ただいま本日二度目（過去通算で１００回目ぐらい）の恋愛相談サミット開催中です。
lines.english: The break after fifth period, in the first-year Class B classroom. Our second romantic-advice summit of the day was now in session. Roughly our hundredth overall.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、まあ、恋するリンダがとつぜん逃げだしちゃった意味不明さはそれでいいとして？」
lines.english: “Okay, so let's say that explains why Linda in Love suddenly ran off for no apparent reason?”

lines.japanese: タマちゃんは手帳をぱたんと閉じました。
lines.english: Tama snapped her notebook shut.

lines.japanese: 「相手があのナンパ先輩ってことは、Ｈさんの彼女が浮気をしていたというのも、どうやら君の早合点のようだねえ？」
lines.english: “If it was that guy who hits on everyone, then it looks like you jumped to conclusions about Mr. Itch's girlfriend cheating on him, too?”

lines.japanese: 「そっかー、そうだね、冤罪だね。うーん、喜んでいいやら悲しんでいいやらだなあ」
lines.english: “Ohhh, right. She's innocent. Hmm, I don't know whether to be happy or sad.”

lines.japanese: 「なんで。べつに喜ぶ要素はないでしょ、だって彼女が浮気してれば、リンダのつけ入る隙があったわけだし」
lines.english: “Why? There's nothing to be happy about, is there? If she was cheating on him, that would've been your chance.”

lines.japanese: 「そうだけど、でも、そんなことになってたら羽田先輩かわいそうだもん」
lines.english: “True, but then I'd feel sorry for Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「ん？　じゃあなに、リンダはふたりの末永い幸せを祈ってるわけ？」
lines.english: “Hmm? So what, you're wishing the two of them a long and happy life together?”

lines.japanese: 「えー、それは困るー」
lines.english: “Nooo, that would be a problem.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあやっぱりＨさんには一回失恋してもらわないと」
lines.english: “Then Mr. Itch needs to get his heart broken once, after all.”

lines.japanese: 「ううー、なんてアンビバレンツな恋なの……」
lines.english: “Ughhh, what an ambivalent love...”

lines.japanese: そんな私の苦悩を目の当たりにすると、タマちゃんは眉をしかめて、結局どうしたいんだと明確な回答を急ぎます。
lines.english: Confronted with my anguish, Tama frowned and pressed me for a clear answer. What did I actually want to do?

lines.japanese: でも私は本当にどうしていいか、どうするべきなのか、矛盾だらけで分からないのです。
lines.english: But I really didn't know what to do, or what I should do. There were so many contradictions.

lines.japanese: 「んっと、あのさ……」
lines.english: “Um, listen...”

lines.japanese: 私がしばらく眉間に皺を寄せて考えていると、タマちゃんが（いつもハキハキしてる彼女にしては珍しく）遠慮がちな声で言いました。
lines.english: While I was frowning and thinking this over, Tama spoke rather tentatively. Unusual for someone who normally says things so clearly.

lines.japanese: 「前々から思ってはいたんだけど、言ってもいい？」
lines.english: “I've been thinking this for a while. Can I say it?”

lines.japanese: 「なに？　いいよ？」
lines.english: “What? Sure?”

lines.japanese: 「恋愛したことないくせにーって思うかもしれないけど、それでも言ってもいい？」
lines.english: “You might think, ‘You've never been in love, what do you know?’ Can I say it anyway?”

lines.japanese: 「いいってばー。どうしたの、親友同士でそんな遠慮しないでよう」
lines.english: “I said you could. What's wrong? We're best friends. Don't be so careful with me.”

lines.japanese: ずばり言いすぎるせいで煙たがられることも多いタマちゃんですが、私は彼女のそういう苦言が決して皮肉や意地悪ではないことを知っているので傷付かないし、むしろ有りがたいとさえ思っているのです。
lines.english: Tama's bluntness often puts people off. But I know that when she tells me things I don't want to hear, she isn't being sarcastic or mean. So it doesn't hurt me. In fact, I'm grateful.

lines.japanese: 「うん、じゃあ言うけど、リンダさ……」
lines.english: “Okay, then. Linda...”

lines.japanese: 「うんうん」
lines.english: “Mm-hmm?”

lines.japanese: 「まだ相手に名前すら知られてない段階なのに、付き合うことになる前提で悩むなんて百年早いと思う」
lines.english: “The guy doesn’t even know your name yet. I think you’re getting a hundred years ahead of yourself, worrying as if the two of you are going to date.”

lines.japanese: 「傷付いた！」
lines.english: “That hurt!”

lines.japanese: 「でも事実でしょ。目つむって夢みたいなこと語ってるより、勇気出して簡単なことから実行した方が建設的なんじゃない？」
lines.english: “But it's true, isn't it? Wouldn't it be more constructive to work up the courage to do something simple, instead of closing your eyes and talking about dreams?”

lines.japanese: 「う、ううっ、タマちゃんのばか！　恋愛したことないくせに！」
lines.english: “U-ugh, you're an idiot, Tama! You've never even been in love!”

lines.japanese: 「そっ、それは言わない約束！」
lines.english: “Y-you promised you wouldn't say that!”

lines.japanese: 「知らないよ！　タマちゃんなんか生涯独身を貫いてひとり寂しく老いさらばえちゃえ！」
lines.english: “I don't care! Stay single your whole life, then! Grow old and wither away all alone!”

lines.japanese: 「え、ちょっ……リンダどこ行くの、六時間目始まる！」
lines.english: “H-hey... Linda, where are you going? Sixth period's starting!”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そっか」
lines.english: “Oh, right.”

lines.japanese: かっこよく教室を飛びだしたかった私ですが、授業をさぼるわけにはいかないのでやめておきました。
lines.english: I'd wanted to make a dramatic exit, but I couldn't skip class, so I gave up on that.

lines.japanese: ちょっと照れくさいというか、ばつが悪いので、さっさとタマちゃんに冗談を交えて謝っておこうと思ったのですが──
lines.english: It was a little embarrassing, or awkward, so I thought I'd apologize to Tama right away with a joke—

lines.japanese: 「リンダってそういうとこ律儀だよね」
lines.english: “You're really conscientious about things like that, Linda.”

lines.japanese: 「ふん、話しかけないで。タマちゃんが謝るまで絶交だもん」
lines.english: “Hmph. Don't talk to me. We're not friends until you apologize.”

lines.japanese: ──つい素直になれず反発してしまいました。
lines.english: —but I couldn't be honest with her, and snapped back instead.
“Haaah...”

lines.japanese: 私ってばかだな。
lines.english: I'm such an idiot.

lines.japanese: 親友のこと、好きなひとのこと、好きなひとの好きなひとのこと……いろんな悩みが頭の中でどろどろ溶けあって、私は気分が悪くなりそうなほど悩みました。
lines.english: My best friend, the person I liked, the person the person I liked liked... All those worries melted into one gooey mess in my head. I worried until I almost felt sick.

lines.japanese: もしこの場にクラスのみんながいなければ、きっとこらえきれず涙がこぼれていたと思います。
lines.english: If the rest of the class hadn't been there, I'm sure I couldn't have held back my tears.

lines.japanese: たぶん私は、日本でいちばん不幸な女の子に違いありません。
lines.english: I was probably the unhappiest girl in Japan.

lines.japanese: 六時間目の授業はまるで頭に入りませんでした。
lines.english: None of the sixth-period lesson sank in at all.

lines.japanese: 「なあ……林田起こしてやった方がいいんじゃねえか？　ノートにヨダレ垂れてんじゃん」
lines.english: “Hey... shouldn't we wake Hayashida up? She's drooling on her notebook.”

lines.japanese: 「いや……でもすげえ幸せそうな顔で寝てるし……」
lines.english: “Yeah... but she looks so happy sleeping...”

lines.japanese: 「きっといい夢見てるんだろうな、林田だから……」
lines.english: “Must be having a good dream. It's Hayashida, after all...”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そっとしといてやろうぜ、林田だから……」
lines.english: “Yeah. Let's leave her alone. It's Hayashida, after all...”

lines.japanese: 私は夢を見ました。
lines.english: I had a dream.

lines.japanese: 何度も再生を繰りかえした記憶。
lines.english: A memory I'd played over and over.

lines.japanese: あれは一年前。遅まきながら、私が本格的に受験勉強を始めたころ。
lines.english: A year ago. When I'd finally started studying seriously for the entrance exams, a little late.

lines.japanese: 突然の大雨、だけど区立図書館は閉館の時刻で、傘を持っていない私はひとり玄関ロビーで途方に暮れていました。
lines.english: Sudden, heavy rain. But the district library was closing, and I stood alone in the entrance lobby with no umbrella and no idea what to do.

lines.japanese: 前門の大雨、後門の『蛍の光』といった状況で、私は馬鹿みたいに何もせず立ちつくしていました。
lines.english: Between the rain and a hard place: a downpour at the front door, the closing strains of ‘Auld Lang Syne’ at my back. I just stood there like an idiot.

lines.japanese: 「ごめんねえ、この雨だから、貸し出し用の傘もぜんぶ出ちゃってて」
lines.english: “Sorry. With all this rain, every umbrella we lend out is already gone.”

lines.japanese: 職員のおじさんが申しわけなさそうな声で私を追いたてます。
lines.english: The man who worked there was apologetically hurrying me out.

lines.japanese: 「まあ、ほら、お母さんに電話して迎えに来てもらえば、ね」
lines.english: “Well, you know. Call your mother and have her come get you, then.”
“Oh, yes...”

lines.japanese: 母はいません。という言葉を呑みこんだつもりが、表情には出てしまったみたいです。おじさんは慌てて違う言い方をしました。
lines.english: I don't have a mother. I thought I'd swallowed those words, but apparently they showed on my face. He hurried to rephrase that.

lines.japanese: 「まあ、あれだね。あのー、おうちのひとがね、あのー、忙しいようだったらね、仕方ないけどね。あのー、まあ、十分ぐらい走ればね、あの、コンビニあるからね。そこで傘買えばね、あのー、悪いけど」
lines.english: “Well, you know. Um, if the people at home are, um, busy, well, there's not much you can do. Um, well, about ten minutes away if you run, there's, uh, a convenience store. You could buy an umbrella there, um, sorry about this.”

lines.japanese: 「はい、そうします。ありがとうございます」
lines.english: “Yes, I'll do that. Thank you.”

lines.japanese: 一生懸命あやまってくれるおじさんに、私は笑顔で答えました。
lines.english: I smiled at the man, who was trying so hard to apologize.

lines.japanese: でもおじさん、ごめんなさい、傘を買うのは勿体ないからコンビニには寄りません。
lines.english: But I'm sorry, sir. Buying an umbrella would be a waste of money, so I won't stop at the store.

lines.japanese: こうなったら、家まで４０分の道のり、朗らかに歌いながらスキップして帰ろう。そのぐらいの覚悟を決めたとき──
lines.english: In that case, I'd skip all the way home, singing cheerfully. All forty minutes of it. Just as I made up my mind—

lines.japanese: ──小さな、だけどとても優しい声が、ふっと後ろから通りすぎてゆきました。
lines.english: —a quiet but very gentle voice slipped past me from behind.

lines.japanese: あげるよ、とか……これいいよ、とか……そんなふうに言ってた気がします。
lines.english: ‘You can have it,’ or... ‘Here, take this,’ or... I think he said something like that.

lines.japanese: 気が付いたらショルダーバッグの肩紐の根本に、男ものの傘が一本ぶらさがっていました。
lines.english: When I looked, a man's umbrella was hanging from the base of my shoulder bag's strap.
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 突然のことに驚いて、一瞬反応が遅れました。
lines.english: It was so sudden that surprise delayed my response for a moment.

lines.japanese: 私が傘を手に取って正面へ向きなおったときには、もうその持ち主はどしゃ降りの雨の中を駆けだしていました。
lines.english: By the time I'd taken the umbrella and turned back toward the door, its owner was already running out into the pouring rain.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そうかよかった、羽田君に傘を借りたんだね」
lines.english: “Oh, good. You borrowed an umbrella from Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「羽田、さん……？」
lines.english: “Haneda...?”

lines.japanese: 「うん。美空学園の羽田君。よく来るわけじゃないんだけど、なかなか面白い子でね」
lines.english: “Yes. Haneda, from Misora Academy. He doesn't come that often, but he's quite an interesting boy.”

lines.japanese: そのときにはすでに背中すら見えなくなっていました。
lines.english: By then, I couldn't even see his back anymore.

lines.japanese: 「ありがとう、ございます……」
lines.english: “Thank you... very much...”

lines.japanese: 私は聞こえるはずのない声を雨の向こうに送りました。
lines.english: I sent my voice out through the rain, where he couldn't possibly hear it.

lines.japanese: 「リンダ起きろー。さっきの謝るからー」
lines.english: “Linda, wake uuup. I'll apologize for earlier.”

lines.japanese: 「……て、なんだ、起きてたの？」
lines.english: “...Oh, what? You were awake?”

lines.japanese: 「私、思いだした……」
lines.english: “I remembered...”

lines.japanese: 「は？　なにが？　あれ、絶交は？」
lines.english: “Huh? What? Wait, weren't we not friends?”

lines.japanese: 「そうだよ、私まだ何にも始まってなかった。タマちゃん、目を覚まさせてくれてありがとう」
lines.english: “Right. Nothing had even started yet. Tama, thank you for waking me up.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、いま君、自分で起きたよ」
lines.english: “No, you just woke up on your own.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、決めた私、先輩に傘のお礼いってくる。それで、自分の名前言って、もう知ってるけど先輩の名前も聞いて、あと、えっと、なんか色んな話とかして……」
lines.english: “Yeah, I've decided. I'll go thank him for the umbrella. Then I'll tell him my name, and ask his name, even though I already know it, and, um, talk about all kinds of things...”

lines.japanese: 「とにかく前に進んでみる！」
lines.english: “I'll just try moving forward!”

lines.japanese: 「え？　ああ、そう？　あれ？　どういう心境の変化？」
lines.english: “Huh? Oh, really? Wait. What brought this on?”

lines.japanese: 「タマちゃんが私のこと怒鳴りちらして引っぱたいてくれたおかげだよ！　ありがとう！」
lines.english: “It's all thanks to you yelling at me and slapping me, Tama! Thank you!”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そんなことしてない！」
lines.english: “I-I didn't do that!”

lines.japanese: 私は走りました。
lines.english: I ran.

lines.japanese: 未来という名の廊下を走りました。
lines.english: I ran down the hallway called the future.

lines.japanese: 学年主任の先生に怒られて途中ちょっと歩いたりもしたけれど、基本的には走りました。
lines.english: The teacher in charge of our grade scolded me, so I walked for a little while along the way, but mostly I ran.

lines.japanese: 明るい未来が見えそうな気がしたんです。
lines.english: I felt as though I might be able to see a bright future.

lines.japanese: でも、やっぱり──
lines.english: But, of course—

lines.japanese: ──現実というのはそんな甘いものじゃなかったんです。
lines.english: —reality wasn't that kind.

lines.japanese: 「え？　え？　なに？　羽田君……！」
lines.english: “Huh? Huh? What? Haneda...!”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんが彼を呼んでいました。教室を出る寸前だったあの優しい背中が、ゆっくりと振りかえって──
lines.english: Watarai was calling him. That gentle back of his, just about to leave the classroom, slowly turned—

lines.japanese: 「え、なにこれ……くれるの……？」
lines.english: “Huh? What's this... Are you giving it to me...?”

lines.japanese: ──彼女の声に、羽田先輩はとても幸せそうに微笑みました。
lines.english: —and at her voice, Haneda smiled so happily.

lines.japanese: 「え……ほんとに？」
lines.english: “Huh... Really?”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんも同じぐらい嬉しそうに笑っていました。
lines.english: Watarai was smiling just as happily.

lines.japanese: ふたりとも、校内の下世話な噂や私の矛盾した心配なんか気にも留めていない、そんな温かな笑顔でした。
lines.english: Both their smiles were so warm. As though they didn't give a thought to the school's tawdry rumors or my contradictory worries.

lines.japanese: プレゼントの中身までは見てません。でも渡来さんの、あの泣きだしそうなぐらい幸せそうな笑顔を見れば、私には十分すぎるほど分かります。
lines.english: I didn't see what the present was. But that smile of Watarai's, so happy she looked ready to cry, told me more than enough.

lines.japanese: きっと羽田先輩は、宝石の輝きにも等しい何かを贈ったのでしょう。
lines.english: Haneda must have given her something as brilliant as a jewel.

lines.japanese: 「良かったですね……せんぱい……」
lines.english: “I'm happy... for you...”

lines.japanese: 私は鼻声で強がりました。
lines.english: I put on a brave face with a stuffy voice.

lines.japanese: これはきっと、勇気を出して走りだそうとした私に、恋愛の神様がご褒美をくれたのでしょう。
lines.english: Surely the god of love was rewarding me for finding the courage to start running.

lines.japanese: あきらめるという未来を。
lines.english: With a future called giving up.

lines.japanese: 「神様のばかああああ！」
lines.english: “You stuuuupid god!”

lines.japanese: 来るときとは違う意味で廊下を走りました。
lines.english: I ran down the hallway again, but this time it meant something different.

lines.japanese: 「すみません！　ピザとドリアとジャンボパフェと、あとクリームソーダおかわりください！」
lines.english: “Excuse me! Pizza, rice gratin, a jumbo parfait, and another ice cream soda, please!”

lines.japanese: 「あのさ……食でストレスを解消するのもいいけどさ。たぶん後悔するよ、財布か体重計を見たときに」
lines.english: “Listen... eating to relieve stress is all very well, but you'll probably regret it when you look in your wallet or at the scale.”

lines.japanese: 「いいの！　デート代貯金もいらなくなったし、自分磨きも必要なくなったの！　食べて肥えて脂ギトギトになって、日本一のぶさいくになってやるんだもん！」
lines.english: “It’s fine! I don’t need my savings for dates anymore, and I don’t need to work on myself anymore! I’ll eat and get fat and greasy and be the ugliest girl in Japan!”

lines.japanese: 「って言ってるけど……ひよちゃん、どうする？」
lines.english: “That's what she says... Hiyo, what should I do?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いいですいいです。すみません紀奈子さん、いまの注文ぜんぶキャンセルして、カモミールティー持ってきてください」
lines.english: “Oh, never mind, never mind. Sorry, Kinako. Cancel that whole order and bring some chamomile tea, please.”

lines.japanese: 「タマちゃん余計なことしないで！　私もう二度と恋なんてしないからいいの！」
lines.english: “Don't interfere, Tama! It's fine because I'm never falling in love again!”

lines.japanese: 「極端な……」
lines.english: “That's a bit extreme...”

lines.japanese: 「それで一生独身を貫いて、タマちゃんとふたり仲よく老いさらばえていくの！」
lines.english: “Then I'll stay single my whole life and grow old and wither away happily with you!”

lines.japanese: 「ちょっ……巻きこまないでよ！」
lines.english: “Hey... leave me out of it!”

lines.japanese: 「あはは、ひよちゃん楽しいお友達だね」
lines.english: “Ahaha, Hiyo, your friend's fun.”

lines.japanese: そして私たちは女同士で食べて騒いで歌って踊って、その他いろいろして、家に帰ってお風呂に入って寝ました。
lines.english: And so we girls ate and made noise and sang and danced and did all sorts of other things, then went home, took baths, and went to bed.

lines.japanese: なにか夢を見た気もしますがよく覚えてません。
lines.english: I think I dreamed about something, but I don't really remember.

lines.japanese: 次の日、満員電車でまた先輩と遭遇して、やっぱりときめいたりするので、私はまた気持ちも新たに今日から恋をすることにしました。
lines.english: The next day, I ran into him again on the crowded train, and my heart fluttered all over again. So, with a fresh heart, I decided to start being in love again that very day.

lines.japanese: 「そういうことです」
lines.english: “That's how it is.”

lines.japanese: 「復活はやくね？」
lines.english: “That was a quick recovery.”

lines.japanese: 「ねー、ほんと恋愛って意味不明だよねー」
lines.english: “Right? Love really doesn't make any sense, does it?”

lines.japanese: でもとりあえず、いまはこうしてお友達と好きなひとのことできゃーきゃー言ってるだけで幸せなので、しばらくそれでいいやと思いました。
lines.english: For now, though, I was happy just squealing with my friend about the person I liked. I thought that would do for a while.

lines.japanese: いい子にしていれば、恋愛の神様もいつかは私に微笑んでくれることでしょう。
lines.english: If I'm a good girl, surely the god of love will smile on me someday.

lines.japanese: ただ、そのう……贅沢は申しませんが、なるべく早いと嬉しいです。
lines.english: Only, um... I won't ask for too much, but I'd be happy if it were sooner rather than later.
